about: Fleet mass-deployment for hunting (doc 129): the actuated 'organism' rail of ./securax hunt. The amoeba is the offline collector (one host, no server); this GENERATES everything needed to stand up a Velociraptor server and roll clients out at scale — the server config steps, the per-method client rollout (GPO, Intune, SCCM/msiexec, Ansible), and a throttled fleet hunt definition. It PROVISIONS NOTHING itself: generating is safe and offline; standing up a server, pushing an MSI to every endpoint and running a fleet hunt are consequential, so they are the human's approved steps (./securax approve), exactly as the growth map grades them 'assisted'. Binaries are pulled from your internal mirror (SECURAX_HUNT_MIRROR), hash-pinned, so endpoints never egress to a vendor. RBAC and multi-org are the platform's, named here so the fleet is governed from day one. This file is DATA; edit the templates, add your own rollout method, point the mirror at your registry.

server.about: Stand up the Velociraptor server (frontend + GUI + datastore). Run on the always-on node; it is the control plane for the fleet, so give it a standby (the offline-collector mode is the no-server fallback).
steps: velociraptor config generate > server.config.yaml   # then set: GUI bind + a strong admin, Frontend public hostname (a NAME, not an IP), Datastore path on durable storage
velociraptor --config server.config.yaml frontend -v   # runs the server; put it behind your reverse proxy / service manager
velociraptor --config server.config.yaml config client > client.config.yaml   # the client config every endpoint needs
server.rbac: Velociraptor has built-in roles (administrator, analyst, investigator, reader) and multi-org; map each team to a role and, for many business units, an org. These are the platform's RBAC/tenancy services — govern the fleet from day one, do not hand everyone administrator.
server.note: The server is a control-plane single point of failure: keep a standby, back up the datastore, and remember the offline collector needs no server at all (the fallback).

throttle.about: Bulk triage on a large fleet moves terabytes; throttle every fleet hunt so it does not saturate the server or the network.
throttle.note: Tune per your server and link; start conservative and raise it. A KAPE-style file collection on 10k endpoints can be multiple terabytes.

msiexec.name: SCCM / msiexec (Windows MSI)
msiexec.about: Repack the client config into an MSI and push it with SCCM, or install directly. The standard Windows route.
msiexec.template:
# Repack the MSI with your client config (on the server), then host it on your internal share/registry:
#   velociraptor --config server.config.yaml config repack --exe velociraptor-<ver>-windows-amd64.msi client.config.yaml velociraptor-client.msi
# Fetch from the internal mirror (no vendor egress), verify the hash, then install silently:
msiexec /i \\<MIRROR>\velociraptor\velociraptor-client.msi /quiet /norestart
# SCCM: import velociraptor-client.msi as an Application, deploy to the target device collection.

gpo.name: Group Policy (Active Directory)
gpo.about: Assign the MSI by GPO software-installation to an OU, or run a startup scheduled task for a temporary IR push.
gpo.template:
# GPO software installation: Computer Config > Policies > Software Settings > Software installation >
#   New > Package > \\<MIRROR>\velociraptor\velociraptor-client.msi > Assigned. Scope the GPO to the target OU.
# Or a startup script (temporary/IR), from the internal mirror only:
msiexec /i \\<MIRROR>\velociraptor\velociraptor-client.msi /quiet /norestart
# gpupdate /force on a test OU first; confirm the service 'Velociraptor' is running before widening scope.

intune.name: Microsoft Intune (Win32 app)
intune.about: Wrap the MSI as a Win32 app (.intunewin) and deploy to an Entra device group.
intune.template:
# Package: IntuneWinAppUtil.exe -c <folder with the MSI> -s velociraptor-client.msi -o <out>
# Intune > Apps > Windows > Add > Windows app (Win32) > upload the .intunewin.
# Install command:   msiexec /i velociraptor-client.msi /quiet /norestart
# Uninstall:         msiexec /x velociraptor-client.msi /quiet /norestart
# Detection rule: service 'Velociraptor' exists / the client binary present. Assign to the target device group.

ansible.name: Ansible (Linux & Windows)
ansible.about: Config-package the binary and push it as a managed service with a playbook — good for Linux fleets and mixed estates.
ansible.template:
- name: Deploy Velociraptor client from the internal mirror
  hosts: endpoints
  become: true
  vars:
    mirror: "{{ securax_hunt_mirror }}"      # your internal registry base, no vendor egress
    sha256: "<PINNED_SHA256>"
  tasks:
    - name: Fetch the client binary (hash-pinned)
      get_url:
        url: "{{ mirror }}/velociraptor/velociraptor-client"
        dest: /usr/local/bin/velociraptor-client
        checksum: "sha256:{{ sha256 }}"
        mode: "0755"
    - name: Install the client config
      copy: { src: client.config.yaml, dest: /etc/velociraptor/client.config.yaml, mode: "0640" }
    - name: Install and start the service
      shell: /usr/local/bin/velociraptor-client --config /etc/velociraptor/client.config.yaml service install
      args: { creates: /etc/systemd/system/velociraptor_client.service }
